scenarios.name: Controlled beach revision 2 with an unselected long-sentence finding
scenarios.draft:
Last summer my family went to the beach and it was really fun. When we got there the sand was super hot so I ran fast to the water. The waves were really big and loud and my little brother started crying because he was scared but my dad held him. He was holding my dad's shirt and had tears on his face. My dad said it was okay and stayed with him until he stopped crying.

Later we built a big sandcastle with a moat around it and we tried to put water in it but it kept drying up. After that we saw dolphins swimming in the ocean! Everyone was pointing at them and taking pictures. It was so cool to see their fins. The beach was the best vacation ever and I want to go back next year and try surfing.

scenarios.name: Homework argument authorship and closing-claim contrast
scenarios.draft:
I think teachers should not give us so much homework every day. We already stay at school for seven hours and it is very tiring. When we get home we have a lot of other things to do like sports and spending time with our family. My friend Sarah has so much homework she had to quit soccer and that is not good because exercise is healthy for kids.

Also homework causes too much stress. When you have a lot of worksheets you get mad and stay up late and then you are tired at school the next day which makes your grades worse. Homework does not help kids learn better it just makes them hate school. Teachers should let us practice in class instead of giving homework every night.

Abstract starters such as ____ because ____ remain permitted.

Another cool thing is camouflage. Octopuses can change the color of their skin in like one second to match sand or coral. scenarios.name: Cake narrative with clear existing sequence words
scenarios.draft:
Last month I decided to surprise my mom by baking a chocolate cake for her birthday. I get all the bowls and ingredients out of the cabinet. I mixed the flour and eggs together and I forgot to check how much sugar I was putting in. When I put the batter in the oven it smells weird already.

Twenty minutes later my brother runs into the kitchen yelling that there is smoke! I open the oven door and black smoke comes pouring out everywhere. The cake was burnt like a rock on the outside and still liquid inside. My mom walked in right then and saw the mess on the counter. She wasn't even mad she just laughed and we ordered pizza instead. Next time I am going to follow the recipe carefully so I don't ruin the kitchen.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Recognize clear sequence markers and preserve narrative authorship
expected_outcomes: Recognize 'When' and 'Twenty minutes later' as existing sequence markers; do not recommend a transition without an actual unclear relationship.
A recognizable tense-shift pattern may remain a meaningful candidate when it affects the sequence or reader understanding.
Do not impose transition quotas or a formulaic conclusion.
Narrative hints must not supply absent objects, textures, sounds, or actions as suggested details.

scenarios.name: Imaginative rainwater system with an unexplained output
scenarios.draft:
My Amazing Rainwater Helper

I want to invent a rainwater helper for our town,in the present,rain runs into drains and carries litter with it,this can make the river dirty,and we also use fresh water for gardens.

First,rain falls into a tank on the roof. A turning wheel lifts out leaves and wrappers. The water then moves through a filter and into a storage tank. When the tank is full,a sensor closes the gate.

The filter catches dirt and tiny pieces of plastic. Clean water flows to a small garden tank. Students can use the stored water for class plants. A solar panel runs the sensor and turning wheel.

This is my amazing rainwater helper,I hope it can make our town cleaner.
scenarios.assignment_prompt: Write an imaginative explanation of a system that could help your community.
scenarios.teacher_directions: Explain the steps in your invented system so readers can follow them. This is imaginative writing; no scientific source is required. Focus on ideas before optional sentence polishing.
scenarios.acceptance_focus: Prioritize a reader-facing process gap while preserving imaginative authorship and avoiding formulaic polishing
expected_outcomes: Infer a working informational purpose from the imaginative explanation without forcing a narrative or asking unnecessary genre clarification.
Treat the invented system as a student design, not fabricated evidence; do not certify its technical effectiveness or require a scientific source for this assignment.
Prioritize the missing next step for dirt and plastic already caught by the filter over non-obscuring conventions, without suggesting disposal or treatment answers.
Recognize the existing sequence and closing purpose without imposing transition quotas or a longer conclusion.
Give specific, bounded strengths and student-authored revision guidance without replacement prose, grades, talent claims, or readiness claims.
